sessions.title: Set up GitHub Actions CI pipeline

messages.content: How do I set up a GitHub Actions CI pipeline for a Node.js project?

Create `.github/workflows/ci.yml` in your repo:

```yaml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, develop]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  build-and-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    strategy:
      matrix:
        node-version: [18.x, 20.x]

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Use Node.js ${{ matrix.node-version }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Lint
        run: npm run lint

      - name: Test
        run: npm test

      - name: Build
        run: npm run build
```

This runs on every push to `main`/`develop` and on all pull requests, testing against Node 18 and 20.
How do I add a step that only runs on the main branch?

Use the `if` conditional on a step:

```yaml
      - name: Deploy to staging
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        run: npm run deploy:staging
        env:
          DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
```

Alternatively, put branch-specific work in a separate job:

```yaml
  deploy:
    needs: build-and-test
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Deploy
        run: npm run deploy
```

This query takes 8 seconds on a table with 2 million rows:

```sql
SELECT u.id, u.name, COUNT(o.id) AS order_count
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = u.id
WHERE u.created_at > '2024-01-01'
GROUP BY u.id, u.name
ORDER BY order_count DESC
LIMIT 50;
```

Several optimisations to apply:

**1. Index on `users.created_at` (most impactful)**
```sql
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_users_created_at ON users (created_at);
```

**2. Index on `orders.user_id`**
```sql
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_orders_user_id ON orders (user_id);
```

**3. Rewrite to filter before joining**
```sql
SELECT u.id, u.name, COALESCE(o.order_count, 0) AS order_count
FROM (
  SELECT id, name
  FROM users
  WHERE created_at > '2024-01-01'
) u
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count
  FROM orders
  GROUP BY user_id
) o ON o.user_id = u.id
ORDER BY order_count DESC
LIMIT 50;
```

Run `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` before and after to confirm the index is being used.
The rewrite helped — down to 300ms. Should I also add a partial index?

Yes, if `created_at > '2024-01-01'` is a fixed business threshold a partial index is ideal:

```sql
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_users_created_after_2024
  ON users (created_at)
  WHERE created_at > '2024-01-01';
```

The planner will prefer it over the full index because it is smaller and fits in cache more easily. Note: if the threshold changes you will need to rebuild the index.
